question: Is there already a named source-native controlled dependency/autonomous-assurance measurement close enough to the 2026 Hawaiian lobelioid buffering system to identify why interaction-quality change does not propagate to reproductive collapse?

sources_checked.title: Do Hawaiian Lobeliads Need Bird Pollinators to Reproduce? A Test Using Restoration Plantings Where Nectarivorous Honeycreepers are Present and Absent
sources_checked.site_context: Hakalau National Wildlife Refuge restoration plantings on Hawaii Island
reported_links: infrequent visits by Iiwi and Hawaii Amakihi to Clermontia lindseyana and C. pyrularia
Amakihi primarily nectar robbed while Iiwi appeared to provide limited pollinator service
mixed mating with autogamy and xenogamy
under extant field conditions reproduction primarily by autogamy

sources_checked.title: Floral trait evolution and pollination ecology in the Hawaiian lobeliad genus, Clermontia (Campanulaceae)
sources_checked.author: Richard James Pender
reported_links: pollination ecology at Hakalau restoration plantings
Iiwi and Hawaii Amakihi infrequent floral visitation
both honeycreepers ineffective pollinators of the two focal Clermontia species
all four dissertation focal lobeliads significantly pollen limited

sources_checked.title: Can Ornithophilous Hawaiian Lobeliads Produce Seeds in the Absence of Pollinators? A Test Using Clermontia kakeana and Cyanea angustifolia (Campanulaceae)
sources_checked.source_native_result: mean seed counts were not significantly different between open-pollinated and pollinator-excluded flowers in the two studied species, supporting autonomous seed production

sources_checked.title: Evaluating the Qualitative Effectiveness of a Novel Pollinator: a Case Study of Two Endemic Hawaiian Plants
sources_checked.treatment_interpretation: manual self and distance-cross experiment rather than autonomous pollinator-exclusion dependency

new_scientific_reading.supported: Autonomous reproduction is not merely a generic Hawaiian-lobelioid possibility: historical work on two exact 2026 focal Clermontia species at Hakalau reports mixed mating, predominantly autogamous reproduction under extant conditions, limited contemporary bird pollination and significant pollen limitation.
new_scientific_reading.not_supported: The historical work cannot be joined to the 2026 contact/robbing/fruit-seed observations as one tagged causal chain, and no source-native numeric controlled dependency estimand for the same 2026 plants/season has been recovered.
new_scientific_reading.buffer_implication: Autonomous assurance becomes a source-supported candidate buffer for Clermontia lindseyana and C. pyrularia, but it is not established as the cause of the 2026 reproductive resilience and does not cover Cyanea shipmanii.

why_not_admitted: historical and 2026 observations are separated in time and are not the same tagged plants or season
numeric controlled dependency or autonomous-to-supplemental ratio for the 2026 context is not recovered
Cyanea shipmanii lacks an exact-taxon matched historical controlled-dependency source in this named check
pollen limitation plus autogamy does not uniquely separate autonomous assurance from other downstream buffering in the 2026 experiment
next_gate: Treat autonomous assurance as a now source-supported candidate in the Hawaiian lobelioid system, but reopen ABM admission only on same-context numeric controlled dependency/assurance or another direct measurement that distinguishes assurance from non-assurance buffering. Do not transport exclusion results from other lobelioid species.
claim_boundary: This named-source check narrows the candidate buffer set. It does not establish a causal bridge from historical bird extinction to 2026 reproduction, does not identify a universal Hawaiian lobelioid mating system, and does not justify fitting an assurance parameter to the 2026 ABM target.
